Contentexpand_moreexpand_lessLearning objectives and content
    Objectives

 The student:
is familiar with a broad outline of the history of mathematics and its applications, including more recent developments
has some understanding of the mathematical contents of the topics discussed in the broad outline
is familiar with a selected set of historical sources (including understanding their mathematical contents)
is familiar with the more detailed development of at least one field within mathematics, including its mathematical contents
is aware of the relevance of mathematics for scientific and societal developments
is able to answer in writing, and orally, historical questions about mathematics and the role of mathematicians in society on the basis of a literature study
is able to use and properly cite sources in connection with historical questions regarding mathematics

    Content



 


Outline of the history of mathematics
Historical sources
Axioms, the need for proof; the role of the Greeks (Euclid's Elements); modern developments regarding rigor
The development of (non-Euclidean) geometry, numbers and algebra, calculus and analysis; probability and statistics, mathematical modeling.
More recent developments in mathematics and its applications, such as discrete optimization
scientific and societal aspects related to the themes mentioned, e.g., the role of the mathematician in modern society

Practical informationexpand_moreexpand_less    Course module2MBA90    Course typeBachelor College    Credits (ECTS)5 EC    CategoryDeepening    Language of instructionEnglish    Offered byMathematics and Computer Science - Mathematics domain

    RemarkThis course replaces 2WH60    Short promotional description of the courseThis course focuses on the development of mathematics over the centuries and its role in society. It includes getting a feel for the mathematics of earlier times (in particular, numbers and algebra, analysis, geometry, probability and statistics, proofs in mathematics), and furthermore links the mathematics to the people involved and to the societal circumstances. In part of the course you can concentrate on a topic of your own choice. But note: mathematical maturity is required.Course enrolmentexpand_moreexpand_less    OSIRIS StudentYou can register yourself via OSIRIS Student. To do so, go to Enroll / Course.
